message.content: The total number of distinct legal positions that can arise in a standard game of chess is astronomically large—on the order of 10⁴⁶ (roughly 10 to the power of forty‑six). This estimate comes from exhaustive enumeration studies and is often cited as the “Shannon number” for positions. In contrast, the number of possible complete games (sequences of moves from start to finish) is even larger, on the order of 10¹²³.
